title: Burst credit interleaving across route aliases causes transient over-allow and billing undercount
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During high-concurrency failover tests we observed the policy engine allowing brief bursts that exceeded configured per-route and per-key quotas when requests hit route aliases and then were retried/fallbacked. The symptom is a visible delta between counted usage (billing data) and enforcement logs: enforcement admits more requests than billing records, producing underbilling and occasional downstream quota exhaustion for customers when the temporary credit was later reclaimed. This ticket tracks investigation, a proposed fix, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible test that demonstrates over-allow condition in CI with deterministic sharding and route aliasing
Fix merged that ensures per-key/per-route burst credits cannot be applied concurrently across alias path + fallback path
New unit + integration tests added covering alias + fallback + shard boundary scenarios
Monitoring alert detects any future divergence between enforcement-allowed and billing-counted tokens within 60s
Backfill script (if needed) identified or executed to correct underbilled accounts or a documented customer communication plan
steps_to_reproduce: Setup two route aliases A->route-1 and B->route-2 pointing to same org and model variant
Configure per-route burst credits: route-1: 500 burst tokens, route-2: 300 burst tokens; org-level monthly quota: 50M tokens
Start a high-concurrency client that alternates requests between route alias A and B at 200 RPS and artificially delay shard reconciler (simulate network partition)
Observe enforcement logs in /var/logs/policy/eval showing both routes consuming burst credits simultaneously for the same billing key
Check billing pipeline (metering-aggregator) and see undercount compared to enforcement-allowed logs

Curl example (simplified): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer key-x' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"route":"/a","input":"..."}' and alternate to route "/b" rapidly while toggling shard-migration flag via admin API
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01: First reproduced in staging during chaos run (see logs: staging/policy/2026-03-01-05.log)
2026-03-03: Narrowed to code path in policy-evaluator where burst credit allocator uses per-shard non-atomic 'available' snapshot + alias remap that can double-apply during fallback routing
1) Request hits shard S1 for alias A, evaluator deducts from per-route burst pool (writes lease) but does not immediately persist aggregator token for billing until end of request
2) Rapid fallback retry for alias B maps to different logical route that routes to shard S2; evaluator also deducts because per-key local cache has not observed the previous lease write
3) Both requests allowed and billing-aggregator only receives single eventual increment due to dedupe logic downstream, or misses one due to race during shard migration
Heap/profile shows low lock contention but missing cross-shard invalidation path; Redis-based lease writes are currently best-effort with 200ms eventual propagation in our test harness
Related: similar timing pattern seen in ENG-27458 (inconsistent-metering-during-planned-shard-migration) but here the trigger is route alias + fallback rather than explicit shard move
root_cause: A race between burst-credit allocation (fast local decision) and global billing increment (eventual/deduplicated write) with alias-based remapping that can route logically-same billing key to different shards. The policy evaluator uses shard-local optimistic available snapshots and lacks a cross-shard lease/enforcement handshake for alias+fallback sequences.
proposed_fixes: Primary: Introduce a short-lived cross-shard lease reservation step for burst credits when route aliases or fallback policies are in play. Reservation must be synchronously acknowledged before allowing burst consumption.
Secondary: Harden billing-aggregator to accept out-of-order increments and remove dedupe logic that can drop races (with idempotency tokens), while maintaining anti-duplication for retries
Tertiary: Add a per-request metadata tag (enforcement-id) that the billing pipeline uses to reconcile allowed vs counted tokens and surface mismatches within 60s
implementation_plan: 1) Small spike: add unit test to reproduce alias+fallback race locally (1d) — Jonah
2) Change: implement synchronous lease reservation path for burst credits with 50ms timeout; fallback to existing fast path if timeout (2d) — Jonah/Aisha pair
3) Add end-to-end integration tests in staging with chaos toggles for shard propagation latency (1d) — Eng QA
4) Deploy to canary with verbose enforcement/billing diffs logging (canary-1: 10% traffic, 48h), monitor diffs
5) If diffs stable, roll to full prod with 5% step increases and alerting; if regressions, rollback immediately
6) Postmortem and billing reconciliation run if any underbilling confirmed
monitoring_changes: Add enforcement_vs_billing.diff metric (per-org, per-route) and alert if >1000 tokens diff sustained for >60s
Dashboard: 'Burst credit reconciliation' under Billing -> Alerts
Tracing: tag enforcement path with enforcement-id and surface in Tempo traces
